title: Share data and context across organizations with IQ Share (Preview)
author: shiv_narayanan

content.text:
The data needed to answer a business question rarely belongs to one organization. Enterprises depend on suppliers, software providers, research partners, and customers for information that complement their own. Yet getting that data into their workflow often means building another pipeline, maintaining another copy, and reconciling access across organizational boundaries.
Even when the data arrives, its meaning can be left behind. Definitions, assumptions, and usage guidance are shared separately, leaving teams to reconstruct the context before they can put the data to work.
With IQ Share in Microsoft Fabric, now in preview, organizations can share supported Fabric data items, along with context stored in lakehouse files, with recipients in other Fabric tenants. Data stays in the producer's tenant, recipients work in their own Fabric workspace, and producers retain control over access.
Introducing IQ Share
IQ Share brings cross-tenant data and context sharing into a Fabric item-based experience. In this preview, producers can share an entire Lakehouse, Warehouse, and Mirrored Items. For Lakehouses, markdown files can accompany the data with descriptions, business definitions, and instructions that help recipients understand how to use it.
Key Benefits
• Zero-copy sharing. There are no data copies made. Data resides in the data producer’s tenant and shortcuts are created, allowing customers to get access to real time data and insights.
• Collaborate across tenants without provisioning a recipient identity in the producer's tenant.
• Keep shared data connected to its source. Newly added tables in a shared item are automatically reflected for consumers, without a separate export-and-refresh pipeline for the sharing relationship.
• Share meaning alongside data. Include Markdown context files in a Lakehouse so recipients can interpret the data and use that guidance when configuring downstream analytics or AI experiences.
• Manage access through the Share Lifecycle. Producers can review recipient acceptance, revoke access, and configure an expiration date that ends access automatically. They can centrally monitor all the shares from OneLake Catalog. API and CI/CD support is available for creating and accepting Shares.
Use cases
IQ Share can help organizations make partner data usable without replicating data. Enterprise scenarios include:
• Supplier and manufacturer collaboration: Share a curated inventory so a manufacturing partner can analyze supplier data alongside its own production information.
• Data-provider distribution: Deliver a curated lakehouse or warehouse to authorized customers in their Fabric tenants, with accompanying definitions were provided through lakehouse files.
• Joint financial analysis: Share an approved lakehouse with an external advisory team for a time-bound engagement, while the producer manages recipient access and expiration.
• Research collaboration: Share a curated research lakehouse and its data dictionary with another institution, helping researchers combine complementary information across tenants.
Partner Integrations using IQ Share
IQ Share allows partners like EY, TomTom, S&P Global, Financial Fabric, and xMentium to build integrations. TomTom, for example, is bringing its geospatial and transportation intelligence into Fabric through IQ sharing, with available data products discoverable through the OneLake catalog. These integrations will be available soon in OneLake Catalog.
How IQShare works
Terminology
Figure: IQ Share Terminology and their descriptions
Create and accepting a Share
The producer selects a Lakehouse or Warehouse, adds recipients, and sets an expiration. IQ Share generates an invitation that you can share with the consumer. Each invited recipient reviews the Share and selects a destination workspace. Fabric creates a Share Subscription Item and a Mirrored OneLake Item for each shared source item. Mirrored OneLake Item is a read-only item that has Shortcuts to the data.
Figure: Illustration of how Share and Share Subscription enables cross tenant sharing.
Fabric-managed shortcuts reference the producer's data; no guest identity is required in the producer's tenant. Lakehouse Markdown files can supply definitions and usage guidance alongside the data. New tables added or deleted within an already shared item are automatically reflected for consumers. These source changes do not require a separate export pipeline. Adding or removing an entire item reflects on the consumer tenant when consumers refresh Share Subscription.
Managing Shares
You can add recipients anytime or update a share expiration. A configured expiration automatically ends access. Producers can also revoke a recipient or delete the Share.
Getting started
Prerequisites
In the producer tenant, a Fabric administrator must enable Enable Share Item (Preview) and External data sharing tenant setting. In the consumer tenant, an administrator must enable Enable Share Subscription Item (Preview). The producer needs Read and Reshare permissions on the source item. The accepting user needs Contributor access to the destination workspace and must sign in with the identity added to the Share.
Create an IQ Share
In the producer workspace, select New item, then Share (Preview). Name the Share, select the lakehouse or warehouse, add recipients, and configure an expiration if appropriate. Review the selection, create the Share, and send the Share URL to the intended recipients.
Figure: Creating a new IQ Share
Accept an IQ Share
Recipients uses the invitation URL to review the producer’s tenant information, shared content, and expiration, choose a destination workspace, and select Accept and create item. The resulting Share Subscription Item shows the relationship and shared-item status. Use the SQL endpoint to query the shared data. Spark notebooks, semantic models, data agents, and ontologies currently require an intermediate Lakehouse and shortcuts rather than direct use of the Mirrored OneLake Item.
Figure: Accepting an IQ Share
Security and governance considerations
IQ Share shares the whole item, including newly added tables, so review both its current contents and future additions. Confirm recipient identities and organizational sharing policies before sending an invitation.
Plan for lifecycle changes. Revocation, expiration, deletion of the Share, or loss of the Share creator's source access can interrupt consumer access and downstream dependencies. Review acceptance and status in the Share Item, document ownership, and test the end-to-end lifecycle with non-production data.
We are excited to see what you build
IQ Share helps organizations spend less time moving data across boundaries and more time using it together. By bringing whole-item sharing, recipient authorization, and access lifecycle controls into Microsoft Fabric, it simplifies collaboration while keeping the producer in control of the sharing relationship.
Learn more about IQ Share refer to the documentation.
Try the preview with a curated, nonproduction data product and share your feedback through the Microsoft Fabric Community. Your input will help shape the experience as we advance OneLake's vision of a unified data foundation where organizations can bring data and context together for analytics and AI.
